newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real rises 0.16 pct in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real rises 0.16 pct in volatile trade.

text.p: Brazil's real rose 0.16 percent to close at 1.0888 per dollar in volatile trade in the commercial foreign exchange market as players tried to determine the direction of dollar flows, dealers said.
The local currency was traded between 1.0880 and 1.0900 reais per dollar, but recovered from Monday's close due to improved dollar liquidity, dealers said.

Preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts at 1640 local/1940 GMT showed a $85 million surplus, but some dealers said it could turn into a deficit at the end of the day. On Monday, forex contracts posted a $147.3 million deficit.
While dollar liquidity improved on Tuesday, dealers said the real could come under pressure if strong dollar inflows do not return to the market soon.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0914 per dollar, down 0.08 percent. In the parallel market, the real closed steady at 1.135 per greenback.
